About Ramp
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
About The Role
Our ideal candidate has a deep understanding of JavaScript, a passion for web performance, and can creatively come up with solutions to solve customer's needs. Our tech stack currently involves TypeScript, React, Vite, and Ryu, our in-house design system.
Check out our Engineering Blog for more on our tech stack, mission and values!
What You’ll Do
Build!
Design performant, beautiful, and usable interfaces
Collaborate on our technical vision. Lead discussions and implementation of multiple complex projects
Foster a culture of upholding industry-leading UX
Continuously improve our engineering processes, tools, and systems that allow us to scale the code base, productivity, and the team
Recruit, interview and develop your own interview questions, while fostering the culture of excellence, velocity and humility
Inspire and mentor less experienced engineers and interns
What You'll Need
Minimum of 2 years of frontend engineering experience preferred
Proficiency in JavaScript and React
Knack for getting the visuals right
Track record of shipping high-quality products and developing projects at scale
Ability to turn business and product ideas into engineering solutions
Desire to work in a fast-paced environment, continuously grow, and master your craft
Alignment with Ramp’s core values of enabling businesses to grow more by spending less
Benefits Available To All Full-time Ramp Employees (Global)
Flexible PTO
Centralized home-office equipment ordering
Health and wellness stipend
Budget for intra-office travel
Weekly coffee stipend
United States
100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents
One Medical annual membership
401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp
Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)
Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay
Pet insurance
In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more
Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)
Canada
Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life
Life, AD&D, and disability coverage
Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)
Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)
Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay
Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health
United Kingdom
Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite
Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi
Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option
Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay
Referral Instructions
If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.
Other Notices
Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

About NCR Atleos
NCR Atleos, headquartered in Atlanta, is a leader in expanding financial access. Our dedicated 20,000 employees optimize the branch, improve operational efficiency and maximize self-service availability for financial institutions and retailers across the globe.
Job Duties for Software Engineer II
Overall Description
Team member operates with minimal to no supervision in many areas while they still may need some direction in others, especially more complex work.
Generally, work is done on a sub-system or well-defined feature within a product road-map.
Typical Experience Range:
4 to 7 years
Typical Education
Bachelor’s Degree in a Technical Discipline
Functional Competencies
Required Skills:
Have professional experience of developing applications in client server/ n-tier architecture using .Net Technologies like ASP.Net, C#.Net, C++,ADO.Net and XML Web Services.
Experience and demonstrated knowledge with RESTful services
Experience and demonstrated knowledge with SQL and any RDBMs e.g. Oracle, SQL Server.
Knowledge of distributed source version control system (such as Git, BitBucket, etc.) will be considered as an advantage
Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities and delivering on tough deadlines.
Ability and willingness to travel on international assignments.
Have professional experience of developing crystal reports.
Experience in implementing distributed architecture using HADOOP.
Experience in the implementation of TLS 1.2 protocol
Experience in designing user interfaces using Angular,React and Ember
Experience of developing dashboards using Microsoft Power BI tools
Experience in working on Web servers like IIS 6.0, 7.0
Expert level skills in debugging techniques
Skilled in problem solving and troubleshooting with proven ability to enhance and improve existing procedures and practices
Continuous Improvement
Consults with own & other teams to collect feedback on work practices
Recommends new industry-leading practices to improve productivity & efficiency
Reviews code to address issues, using root cause analyses to eliminate them in future
Seeks out novel & efficient ways of working to develop solutions & products that add value to customers
Quality Design & Assurance
Able to communicate operational definition of ‘quality’ to ensure all teams have clear expectations and standards of excellence
Ensures existing processes are followed, identifies new processes as necessary to meet standards of excellence criteria
Works to eliminate critical and high priority defects, ensuring acceptance criteria are met
Understands operational, technical, and functional needs of the product and reviews test cases to deliver a positive end-user experience
Software Design & Development
Consults with internal & external stakeholders to gather understanding of domain, customer & strategic requirements
Effectively translates requirements & user stories into SW design, recognizing where gaps in understanding exist that can impact building of code
Designs beyond scope if necessary to build right solution
Evaluates options for re-use of existing SW to accelerate or improve product delivery
Software Engineering Best Practices
Maintains a deep understanding of the SW development life cycle
Seeks out knowledge and training to remain current on best practices and technologies
Utilizes knowledge of engineering best practices to ensure quality throughout the software development life cycle
Proposes modifications to the life cycle based on lessons learned
Understands industry standards and best practices for quality testing and determines the best way to apply them within the organization
Trouble Shooting
Analyzes customers’ problems & develops testable theories to diagnose solution / product code issues
Utilizes range of strategies, techniques & tools to investigate possible resolutions to solve issues
Determines best possible solution for increasingly complex problems, quickly implementing solution to reduce downtime for customer.

NCR Atleos is an equal-opportunity employer. It is NCR Atleos policy to hire, train, promote, and pay associates based on their job-related qualifications, ability, and performance, without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, citizenship status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, pregnancy, marital status, age, mental or physical disability, genetic information, medical condition, military or veteran status, or any other factor protected by law.
Statement to Third Party Agencies
To ALL recruitment agencies: NCR Atleos only accepts resumes from agencies on the NCR Atleos preferred supplier list. Please do not forward resumes to our applicant tracking system, NCR Atleos employees, or any NCR Atleos facility. About the Company
Careem is building the Everything App for the greater Middle East — making it easy to move around, order food and groceries, manage payments, and more. Our purpose is simple: to simplify and improve people’s lives and build an awesome organisation that inspires.
Since 2012, Careem has enabled earnings for over 2.5 million Captains, simplified the lives of more than 70 million customers, and built a platform where the region’s best talent and entrepreneurs thrive. We operate in 70+ cities across 10 countries, from Morocco to Pakistan.
We’re now entering our next chapter — one powered by AI. We’re looking for AI talent: curious problem-solvers who know how to apply AI to build tools, automate workflows, and create real impact. Whether it’s streamlining operations, enhancing customer experience, or reimagining internal systems — we want people who can make Careem work smarter and move faster.
About The Team
At Careem, the mission for the NextGen Programme is to help grow our engineers by learning how to write Clean Code, use SOLID principle techniques, and design reliable systems. The ultimate goal is to train new engineers to build excellent foundations with high standards. Our Programme covers vast areas in engineering: Backend, Frontend, Web, Mobile, Data Analysis, MLOps, Infrastructure, Cyber Security and QA.
We are looking for software engineers to join our team of talented engineers that share a common interest in distributed backend systems, their scalability, and continued development. You will work alongside a top talent for an accelerated learning path. You will have access to some of the most exciting projects and advanced tech for accelerated learning and exposure.
You will be responsible for maintaining some of our services that power the Careem. Engine, scaling highly distributed systems, and continuously documenting and improving our engineering practices. These large-scale, distributed systems handle everything from user requests to payment processing.
What You'll Do
Our tech stack is Java 8 and Spring Boot, Micro-Service Architecture, SQL and no-SQL DBs and AWS infrastructure. Key responsibilities include:
Development of our distributed backend system to meet the challenging functional, scalability, and reliability requirements for our fast-growing business.
Maintain features and systems, with an emphasis on code quality, maintainability, readability, and testing.
Facilitate collaboration with other engineers, product owners, and designers to solve interesting and challenging problems across our platform.
Be a valued member of an autonomous, cross-functional agile team.
You care about quality and you know what it means to ship high-quality code.
What You'll Need
2-4 Years of Experience required.
The ideal candidate will have a passionate commitment to improving the lives of people, an insane focus on excellence and customer service, and a strong alignment with our core values: being bold, focused, agile and collaborative.
Must Have
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or other related technical fields.
Understanding of Object-oriented design, data structures, and algorithms.
Ability to solve complex problems.
Must be able to write clean and maintainable code (must love coding!).
Ability to effectively articulate technical challenges and solutions; deal with loosely defined problems and fast-changing requirements & think abstractly.
Passionate about learning new technologies and working on a product of massive scale and impact.
Able to communicate effectively.
Attention to detail.
Nice To Have
Knowledge of AWS
Knowledge of clean code principles
Deep understanding of design patterns
Demonstrated ability of test-driven development

About The Role
We’re looking for a product-minded fullstack engineer to build the core experiences that power our AI agents. You’ll work across the stack, from user-facing product experiences to the systems that orchestrate and deploy autonomous agents, partnering closely with Product, Design, and AI/Engineering.
This role can be remote, but you’ll need to work close to Pacific Time (PT) hours to ensure close collaboration with the engineering team.
What You'll Do
Design, build, and iterate on fullstack systems that power AI agents from concept to deployment.
Research and evaluate new approaches to agent orchestration, prompting strategies, and model alignment.
Collaborate with product, design, and engineering teams to improve UX and usability for non-technical users.
Share learnings, document findings, and contribute to the evolution of internal best practices.
Participate in peer reviews, brainstorming sessions, and technical deep dives with our global team.
Ideal Candidates Have
3+ years of experience in a product-oriented software engineering role.
A strong foundation in Typescript, React, NextJS, and NodeJS.
Experience working in fast-paced environments with a track record of rapid learning and iteration.
Interest in research, technical writing, or contributing to knowledge-sharing within a team.
Bonus: experience with large language models, prompt engineering, or AI infrastructure.
Base salary range: $180,000 – $250,000
Final offer will be based on a variety of factors, including role level, relevant experience, skills, and job-related expertise.
11x is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law.

Software Engineer | Meridian Review Group
Remote, London, Prague or Costa Rica | Full-Time or Long-Term Contract | $9,000–$12,000 per month depending on experience
Meridian Review Group is looking for a Software Engineer to join our growing international team and help build the technology behind a rapidly expanding network of independent business, markets and economic publications.
This is a role for someone who wants to build, not simply maintain.
Meridian currently operates specialist publications covering major economies, financial markets, companies, technology, investment and economic change. Our network includes Global Markets Review, British Business Review, American Commerce Review, German Business Review, Dutch Business Review, Czech Business Review and Gulf Business Review .
We are building Meridian as much more than a collection of conventional news websites.
Alongside journalism, we are developing market-data products, company and executive databases, rankings, economic datasets, research tools, structured entity systems, internal editorial technology and new ways for readers to understand companies, industries, markets and economies.
The role can be fully remote or based from one of our locations in London, Prague or Costa Rica .
What We’re Building
Meridian Review Group is an international publishing, research and intelligence group covering business, markets, investment, technology, AI, energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, finance and economic policy.
Our model combines timely journalism with information designed to remain useful long after publication.
That includes:
Company and executive profiles
Market and stock data
Economic and regional guides
Industry directories
Rankings and indexes
Investment trackers
Original research datasets
Company, sector and geographic databases
Searchable reference products
Specialist newsletters and recurring editorial products
Data-backed journalism
Research and intelligence products for professional audiences
The network is already reaching a meaningful audience, but we are building the infrastructure with a much larger goal in mind.
Our ambition is to create a publishing and information platform capable of reaching millions of readers every month , ultimately building toward 10 million monthly visitors across the Meridian network . We currently reach approximately 480,000 readers across our publications in under a year and are growing rapidly.
That creates a very different engineering challenge from building a single publication.
We need systems that can support multiple brands, thousands and eventually hundreds of thousands of content and entity pages, rapidly growing search traffic, structured datasets, financial information, new publications and entirely new research products without the platform becoming increasingly difficult to maintain.
We want to build systems that work well today while being designed for what Meridian could become several years from now.
One Platform, Multiple Publications
One of the more interesting parts of the engineering challenge is that Meridian is not one website.
Much of the network operates from a shared technical foundation, while each publication maintains its own identity, editorial focus, domain, information architecture and audience.
An improvement to the underlying platform might therefore benefit:
Global Markets Review
British Business Review
American Commerce Review
German Business Review
Dutch Business Review
Czech Business Review
Gulf Business Review
and future Meridian publications that have not yet launched.
This creates opportunities to build reusable systems for:
Publishing
Structured data
Company profiles
Authors
Topics
Geographic hubs
Market data
Rankings
Research products
Internal linking
Search
SEO
Analytics
Advertising
Subscriptions
Editorial workflows
while still allowing each publication to evolve independently.
What You’d Work On
There isn’t a narrow list of tickets waiting for you.
You’ll work with our existing engineering, editorial and leadership teams to determine what we should build next and how we should build it.
Depending on your strengths, that could include:
Building new reader-facing products and features
Improving the shared Meridian publishing platform
Building infrastructure that allows us to launch new publications efficiently
Creating tools for journalists, editors and researchers
Building structured company, executive, industry and economic databases
Developing market-data infrastructure
Creating stock and company information products
Building APIs and data pipelines
Integrating external financial and economic datasets
Building ranking and index products
Developing systems for original Meridian research
Improving article discovery and recommendation
Building stronger topic, company, sector and geographic architecture
Developing search and research functionality
Improving technical SEO and Core Web Vitals
Building entity-based internal linking systems
Developing automated publishing and editorial workflows
Creating internal monitoring and intelligence tools
Building systems to monitor data freshness and accuracy
Automating indexing, canonical, redirect and orphan-page audits
Improving analytics and understanding how readers interact with the network
Experimenting with AI-assisted research, classification and editorial tooling
Building future subscription and premium research products
Developing infrastructure for advertisers and commercial products
Some projects will be highly visible.
Others might remove hours of repetitive editorial work or quietly improve thousands of pages across the network.
Both matter.
Building for Scale
A major part of this role is helping us prepare Meridian for a much larger audience.
We want the network to be technically capable of supporting 10 million monthly visitors as the publications grow.
This is not simply a traffic problem.
Growth means considerably more:
Articles
Companies
Executives
Stock pages
Geographic pages
Industry pages
Rankings
Datasets
Publications
APIs
Internal relationships between entities
Search-engine crawling
Data updates
Editorial activity
That means thinking seriously about:
Performance under significantly higher traffic
Efficient rendering and caching
Database and API performance
Infrastructure reliability
Search and indexing at very large content volumes
Programmatic page generation
Cost-efficient scaling
Monitoring and observability
Content delivery architecture
Data freshness
Search-engine crawl efficiency
Resilience during major market or breaking-news traffic spikes
Shared infrastructure across multiple domains
Preventing architectural decisions that work for seven publications but become problematic at twenty
We do not expect every engineer to arrive having built a 10-million-user publishing platform.
We do want people who understand the difference between building something that works and building something that can continue working as usage, data and complexity increase dramatically.
Data Is Becoming a Major Part of Meridian
Meridian is increasingly building products where journalism and structured information sit alongside one another.
Global Markets Review, for example, incorporates company and market information.
Across the wider network we are developing products including company databases, executive profiles, economic datasets, investment trackers, rankings and proprietary research.
Examples include research and data projects around:
AI adoption
Corporate leadership
Gulf AI and infrastructure investment
Companies and markets
Regional economies
Technology ecosystems
Investment
Energy and infrastructure
We expect this side of Meridian to expand considerably.
Some products may begin as datasets used by journalists.
Others may become searchable public resources.
Some may eventually become subscription or professional intelligence products.
Engineering will play a major role in determining how those systems are designed.
Building an Entity-Based Publishing Platform
One particularly important engineering direction for Meridian is structured information.
An article about a company should not exist in isolation.
That company might also connect to:
Its company profile
Executives
Stock information
Headquarters
Countries and cities
Industries
Competitors
Rankings
Investment activity
Previous Meridian coverage
Relevant economic indicators
Research datasets
The same applies to people, industries, regions and markets.
Over time we want Meridian to become increasingly good at understanding and representing those relationships.
That creates interesting engineering problems around databases, entity resolution, structured data, search, internal linking, page generation and information architecture.
The Kind of Engineer We’re Looking For
We’re less interested in finding somebody who matches a rigid technology checklist than somebody who can look at a problem, understand why it matters and work out a sensible way to solve it.
You’ll probably enjoy this role if you like a relatively high level of ownership.
We’re particularly interested in engineers who:
Have built real production software used by real users
Are comfortable moving between frontend and backend problems
Can understand an unfamiliar codebase quickly
Care about performance, reliability and maintainability
Think about scale rather than only immediate implementation
Understand databases and structured information
Enjoy solving ambiguous problems rather than only executing predefined tickets
Can explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers
Are interested in publishing, markets, research, data or information products
Understand that SEO can be an engineering problem as much as a marketing problem
Know when a simple solution is better than an elaborate one
Are comfortable working asynchronously with an internationally distributed team
Like experimenting, but can distinguish useful experimentation from unnecessary complexity
Are interested in building systems that may eventually serve millions of users
You do not need previous experience working for a newspaper or media organisation.
Experience building SaaS products, research platforms, financial products, data products, marketplaces, content systems or startup products could all translate particularly well.
Technology
Our current environment includes technologies and tools such as:
TypeScript
JavaScript
React
Next.js
Node.js
Git and GitHub
Vercel
SQL and modern databases
REST APIs
Structured data
Analytics infrastructure
Modern web performance tooling
Technical SEO systems
AI APIs and automation workflows
External financial, market and economic datasets
Experience across the entire stack is not expected.
Strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity and the ability to learn quickly matter considerably more than having every technology on your CV.
Engineering Inside a Publishing and Research Group
One of the things that makes this role different is the proximity between engineering and the rest of Meridian.
You won’t be several layers removed from the people using what you build.
An editor might identify a research process that takes several hours and could be automated.
A financial dataset might need to update thousands of company pages.
A new ranking might require its own methodology, database and publishing architecture.
A new Meridian publication might need country, company, topic and city infrastructure before launch.
Search data might reveal an entirely new information product worth building.
An internal dataset might become valuable enough to turn into a public research platform.
We want engineering involved in those conversations early.
The best solution may be a new application.
Sometimes it might be an API, an automation, a database, an interface or twenty lines of code that eliminate an unnecessary workflow.
A Small Team With Real Ownership
Meridian remains small enough that individual engineers can have a substantial effect on the product.
You won’t be engineer number 400 responsible for maintaining one subsection of one product.
You’ll be able to influence architecture, propose products, question existing systems and take ownership of meaningful parts of Meridian’s technical roadmap.
That might mean owning a research product.
It might mean redesigning part of the publishing architecture.
It might mean developing Meridian's market-data infrastructure.
It might mean building the system that allows us to launch the next ten publications.
We want people who see things that should exist and are comfortable helping us build them.
Location and Working Structure
The position can be:
Fully remote
Based from London
Based from Prague
Based from Costa Rica
Our wider team is internationally distributed, so much of our collaboration is already designed around remote and asynchronous work.
The position can be structured as either a full-time role or a long-term contract , depending on location and circumstances.
Expected compensation is $9,000–$12,000 per month , depending on experience, technical depth and level of responsibility.
Why Meridian?
We are still early enough that many of the most interesting systems have not been built yet.
The opportunity is not simply to maintain several news websites.
It is to help build the technical infrastructure behind an international network of business, markets and economic publications.
We believe modern publishing can combine journalism with structured information, proprietary research, useful datasets and software products far more effectively than most traditional publications currently do.
The distinction between a publication, research platform and information product is increasingly blurry.
We see that as an opportunity.
Growing Meridian toward 10 million monthly visitors will require much more than producing more journalism.
It will require better discovery systems, stronger information architecture, faster infrastructure, better data models, automated workflows, deeper products and technology capable of supporting substantially larger audiences.
At the same time, Meridian itself can become much larger.
Seven publications do not necessarily need to remain seven.
The underlying platform should make it possible to expand into new markets, industries and specialist subjects without rebuilding the organisation's technology every time.
That is the problem we want this engineering team to help solve.
The right engineer will have an unusual opportunity to influence what that platform ultimately becomes.
Applying
Apply through the LinkedIn application on this listing.
Please include:
Your current location
Whether you prefer remote work, London, Prague or Costa Rica
Examples of products, systems or projects you have built where relevant
You do not need to match every technology or requirement above.
We would rather speak with a strong engineer who has built interesting things, thinks independently and wants substantial ownership than someone whose CV simply contains every keyword in our stack.
Meridian Review Group
https://meridianreviewgroup.com

Job Description
We are seeking a technically strong Distributed Cache & Java Support Engineer to support distributed caching solutions and onboard Java and Spring Boot application use cases to the distributed-cache platform.
The candidate will combine hands-on Java development with practical enterprise distributed cache or in-memory data grid experience.
The role focuses on cache use-case assessment and onboarding, Java integration support, distributed-cache troubleshooting, and JVM diagnostics.
Key Responsibilities
Provide production support for distributed cache clusters and related Java application integrations
Monitor cluster health, partition distribution, memory, latency, throughput, capacity, and performance
Support cache configuration and troubleshooting across distributed maps, Near Cache, eviction and expiry/TTL, partitioning, backup and replication, serialization, and cluster discovery
Diagnose cache-related incidents including high latency, memory pressure, member restarts, split-brain conditions, data inconsistency, and degraded performance
Coordinate with application, infrastructure, and vendor support teams to investigate issues and drive technical resolution
Review and modify Java or Spring Boot code required to onboard application use cases to the distributed-cache platform
Work with application teams to understand the use case, data model, access pattern, expected load, and caching objectives
Implement application-side cache integration changes and validate serialization, distributed maps, Near Cache, eviction/TTL, and client configuration
Troubleshoot JVM and application issues encountered during onboarding, integration testing, and production stabilization
Minimum Qualification & Experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science, Software Engineering, or Information Technology
7+ years of relevant experience in Java backend development, Java application support, distributed systems, or closely related engineering work
3+ years of hands-on experience with distributed caching or in-memory data grid technologies in conjunction with Java applications
Must Have
Strong hands-on Java development experience, including the ability to write and modify Java code
Strong JVM troubleshooting capability, including memory management, garbage collection, thread dumps, heap analysis, and performance diagnosis
Hands-on Spring Boot development or application-support experience, including cache integration or use-case onboarding
Hands-on experience with any distributed caching or in-memory data grid technology such as Redis, Hazelcast, Apache Ignite, Ehcache, Oracle Coherence, Infinispan, Memcached, or comparable platforms. Training will be provided on the selected platform.
Strong understanding of distributed maps, Near Cache, eviction/expiry/TTL, partitioning, backup/replication, split-brain, serialization, and cluster discovery
Good to Have
Production application support experience in banking, telecom, or other mission-critical environments, including incident triage, root cause analysis, and documentation
Basic support-level exposure to Kubernetes, containers, Linux, networking, and optionally Anthos or OpenShift; deep platform expertise is not required
Familiarity with CI/CD processes and deployment-pipeline troubleshooting
Experience with Splunk, AppDynamics, or Hazel cast Management Center, plus basic TLS/mTLS and certificate troubleshooting.

Who WE are?
KAVAK is the number one e-commerce in the purchase and sale of pre-owned vehicles with the fastest growth in Latin America. We work smart and make things happen, offering the easiest, safest and most transparent experience to buy or sell a car .
But our journey doesn't stop there: at KAVAK our goal is global! Now our footprint extends to the vibrant GCC region as part of our expansion into the Middle East, in the pursuit of our one and only goal: to transform the automotive market around the world.
Today we have more than 180 Kavakees on the GCC team and growing, surrounding ourselves with the best talent to continue building the technology, processes, and products that make us the number one player in the pre-owned car market .
Wanna join us on this exciting ride?
Job Description
This is a remote position open to candidates based anywhere in PAKISTAN ONLY .

At Zyte, we don't just collect web data—we solve complex web data challenges at scale. We are a globally distributed team that is bold, curious, and dedicated to building innovative ways to deliver clean, reliable web data from across the internet.
Data is our passion: We unlock access to open web data, empowering organizations—from startups to global enterprises—to power competitive intelligence, analytics, and AI pipelines
Remote-first culture: Work from anywhere in the world. With over 260 Zytans across 33 countries, our strength comes from diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills
Engineering excellence: We love diving deep into complex code bases, evaluating emerging technologies, and pushing technical boundaries. If you thrive on creative problem-solving and reliably delivering production-grade solutions, you will fit right in
Established system design framework: We systematically analyze functional and product requirements alongside architectural trade-offs to make informed, sustainable design decisions
Real-world distributed systems challenges: Tackle rare engineering problems in custom networking, high-throughput streaming, and large-scale orchestration under real-world operational constraints
Strong product ownership: Work on a profitable, market-leading platform with dedicated time and resources allocated for architectural research and strategic feature engineering
Why This Role?
Zyte API fetches the web through a ladder of routes: plain HTTP, headless browsers, and, for the hardest targets, Edge—our own residential network of real devices. Edge is the tier that must succeed when everything else has failed. Today, a Rust peer on residential Windows PCs long-polls a single command-and-control service (CNC) over mTLS gRPC; CNC schedules fetches onto peers, runs a CONNECT proxy gateway, owns geo-routing, per-site cooldowns, and bandwidth quotas. It must grow from thousands of nodes to tens of millions of requests a day with rock-solid reliability.
The Edge Platform squad owns the control plane and data plane of this residential stack across Windows, Android, and Linux. The next step is building a proper Fleet Manager: a control plane with provider adapters (volunteer PCs, mobile-IP device farms, self-hosted nodes), a reconciler, rollout control, and metrics export sitting beside CNC as the data plane. You will design and operate that system—handling the scheduling, networking, proxying, and reliability work that turns residential devices into infrastructure other squads depend on. You will work directly with the Team Lead, a Principal Engineer, and partner engineering squads across Zyte.
What You'll Do
Scale the data plane. Evolve CNC from a single-replica service into a horizontally scalable fetch scheduler: node selection that respects geo, site cooldowns, jail and per-peer quotas while avoiding detectable patterns, at 50-100M requests per day
Build the Fleet Manager control plane. Design and ship the inventory, health, configuration and software-rollout plane for the fleet: provider adapters, a reconciler, a rollout controller and an exporter to BigQuery, so a second device provider can be onboarded without bespoke scripts
Own the proxy path. Operate and improve the CONNECT proxy gateway and session handling on the edge, and work with the API squad on IP reputation, proxy leases and request scheduling so Edge slots cleanly into the platform's proxy plane
Engineer the networking. mTLS gRPC between control plane and peers, long-poll and streaming semantics over unreliable residential links, NAT and carrier-grade NAT behaviour, and bandwidth accounting that is correct under contention
Make it reliable. Define SLOs for availability, success and latency of the Edge route; build the metrics on peer count, drop-off and bandwidth that hold us and our supply partners accountable; run blue/green rollouts of CNC and peers safely
Share production ownership. Take part in the squad's on-call rotation, lead incident post-mortems and turn operational lessons into platform improvements
Raise the bar. Write RFDs for scheduling, fleet management and failover; review designs across the squad; and bring distributed-systems rigour (consistency, backpressure, idempotency, blast radius) to a young codebase
Requirements
Who You Are
5+ years of production Rust experience, shipping and operating services you own end to end
Distributed systems: you have designed and run schedulers, control planes or stateful services at scale, and can reason about consistency, partitions, backpressure and idempotency without a whiteboard
Deep networking: TCP, TLS and HTTP at the handshake and packet level, gRPC and long-lived connections across NAT and lossy links, and what a client looks like on the wire
Proxy expertise: you have built or operated forward proxies, proxy gateways or residential/ISP proxy infrastructure, and understand IP reputation, session stickiness and pool health
Ops and reliability experience: SLOs and error budgets, observability you built yourself, production incidents you led, and comfort with being on call
Cross-platform awareness: comfortable with Rust running on Windows, Linux and Android targets, and with FFI boundaries when the data plane needs them
Async communication: strong written communication for a globally distributed, remote-first environment
Curious problem solver: you like finding out why a system behaves the way it does under load, and fixing the cause rather than the symptom
Our Tech Stack
Languages: Rust (tokio, tonic), C++ (Cronet) at the peer boundary; Python and Java in the services we integrate with
Protocols: gRPC and protobuf over mTLS, HTTP CONNECT proxying, the Chromium network stack and our own browserless HTTP client
Infrastructure: GCP and Kubernetes for the control plane, Terraform, blue/green deployments; multi-cloud (OCI, GCP) and data centres (Hetzner, Servers.com) across the wider platform
Data & Messaging: Valkey, BigQuery, Confluent Kafka
Monitoring & Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, OpenTelemetry
Bonus Points
Mobile or desktop Rust: experience shipping Rust on Android, Windows or macOS, or binding Rust to C/C++ via FFI
Fleet or device management: reconcilers, rollout controllers, IoT or volunteer-computing fleets
Anti-bot and fingerprinting: understanding of how TLS, HTTP and IP signals are used to classify traffic
Web scraping & crawling experience: familiarity with the technical challenges of large-scale web data extraction
Open source contributions: history of contributing to Rust, networking or distributed-systems open-source projects
Why Join Us?
Impact at scale: Build the residential network tier behind web-scale data pipelines for top-tier global enterprises
Autonomy and flexibility: Enjoy a genuine remote-first culture with flexible working hours and high organizational trust
Continuous innovation: Solve emerging, complex technical challenges as AI and web data extraction rapidly evolve
Global community: Collaborate with a passionate, diverse team of distributed systems engineers and data specialists across the world
If you are a Rust engineer who wants to turn tens of thousands of residential devices into dependable infrastructure, we would love to hear from you. Join us in building the fleet behind web data extraction at Zyte.

Have the freedom and flexibility to work from where you do your best work
Attend conferences and meet with team members from across the globe
Work with cutting-edge open source technologies and tools

China produces about 85% of the world's cathode active material. The West needs new battery chemistries to compete, but traditional R&D can take years to deliver them. 
 
Today, we announced $45M in funding to change that. 
 
Backed by  Zone II Ventures, and Course Corrected, we're scaling our AI-powered Discovery Engine, which combines 18 years of proprietary battery data with automated labs that physically build and test new materials. Over these 18 years our platform has run more than 225 projects for more than 85 customers across the battery value chain, including nearly a dozen Fortune 500 companies, and has resulted in more than 100 battery patents.  Along the way, the platform generated an internally consistent dataset covering more than 500,000 physical cells tested at over 165 million cycles.  
 
Our technology has already helped deliver DRX, a new family of nickel- and cobalt-free cathode materials designed to reduce dependence on China. Now, we're bringing DRX toward commercialization while using AI to accelerate the next generation of breakthroughs. 
 
Led by founder and CEO Mathias Ingvarsson, COO and former Tesla manufacturing leader Steven Prast, and Chief Scientific Officer Dee Strand, we're building a faster path from battery discovery to commercial deployment. 
 
Read more in Fortune by Nick Lichtenberg. Article link in the first comment.

XBOX is building a new kind of flywheel with games at the center.

The company announced XP this morning (a clever title)—a new division headed by Kayleen Walters focused on creating more on-ramps for fans to its beloved IP through film & television, consumer products, live events, and strategic partnerships.

Here are the four divisions:

* XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling. 
* XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love. 
* XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations. 
* XBOX PARTNERSHIPS: Working with creators, brands, and communities to develop new experiences, sponsorships, and brand partnerships.

The move—championed by Matthew Ball following an internal memo from Asha Sharma—is both elegant and strategic. It adopts the best strategies from Disney and Nintendo, both of whom understand that content is king. Where Disney’s flywheel was built strategically around film and television firs, Nintendo’s is game first.

With this move, XBOX is positioning itself to move beyond being a mere platform to owning its market position as both a publisher and steward of massive IP (from Minecraft to Halo and beyond).

I’m excited to see where this leads.

BREAKING: Brookfield announces HUGE $27 BILLION AI data centre project in the UK! 

Brookfield has partnered with British energy company Drax Group and AI business Radiant to develop one of the UK’s largest AI data centres at Drax Power Station in the north of England. 

Bloomberg reports that the project could attract more than $27 Billion billion in investment, with an initial $3.3 Billion planned for the first phase, backed by Brookfield’s partnership with the Qatar Investment Authority.

The idea is to build the data centre alongside an existing power station, giving it access to the enormous amounts of electricity needed to run AI technology. Drax CEO Will Gardiner said: “If constructed in full, this project could become one of the largest data centres in the UK.” Brookfield's Connor Teskey recently said of AI infrastructure: "there is no shortage of capital - and there is no shortage of demand."

Big news for European AI infrastructure!

Clarification: On Thursday, Oct. 15, thousands of Aggie students took part in TWO major marches to downtown Greensboro:

- The first was a March to the Polls, as previously described, which went from campus to the Union Square polling location downtown on the first day of early voting in North Carolina. Students marched back to campus after voting in protest of the Guilford County Elections Board's removal of their campus early voting polling location earlier this year.

- The second was a March for Justice for Nolan Wells, the 18-year-old young man who tragically died July 4 under murky circumstances in the waters off Mississippi’s Horn Island after celebrating the Independence Day holiday. The march was organized by the A&T chapter of the NAACP, and a coalition of groups worked tirelessly to bring students together in solidarity for Nolan from across campus and the entire state. The march began at A&T’s February One monument, went downtown to the International Civil Rights Museum and returned to campus.

Incredibly, thousands of Aggies took part in *both* marches, but in the video posted here, were returning from the second march, which concluded later. In both instances, outstanding civic leadership and participation were on full display from A&T students in the best tradition of Aggies, who have been leading in important community events since the university’s establishment in 1891. 

A&T continues to be America's largest HBCU, as well as its top-rated public HBCU in Forbes and US News & World Report.

At 20:05 UTC on October 29, approximately USD 6.36 billion began moving out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes. It is the largest crypto theft on record, roughly four times the Bybit hack of February 2025.

TRM Labs attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite state-sponsored hacking unit, based on robust on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The same group was named by the FBI in the Bybit hack, and the staging, the Tornado Cash funding and the pre-signed transactions all match earlier North Korea-linked heists.

The response has been fast. Tether, Circle, Ripple, World Liberty Financial and Arbitrum’s Security Council have frozen roughly USD 2.7 billion. But the attacker still controls about USD 2.4 billion in assets beyond any issuer’s reach, and is racing to convert and move them.

TRM continues to work with Binance and the Beacon Network to track the funds and alert partners in real time. The story is still developing, and we will share more as the investigation unfolds.
